in_hebrew.name: הננדייה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם הננדייה הוא שילוב של שני מילים עבריות: הנן ודיה. הנן פירושו חסד או חן, ודיה הוא שורש שפירושו יד או האל. לכן, הננדייה יכולה להתפרש כמי שמקבלת חסד אלוהים או כמי שיד אלוהים היא עמה. השם מופיע בשינויים שונים בתנך, אך לא בצורה זו בדיוק. השימוש בשם זה הוא בעיקר במסגרת השמות הנוצריים והוא מיועד לתאר את הקשר בין האדם לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Χανναδιά
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Χανναδιά προέρχεται ἀπό τὶς ἑβραϊκὲς λέξεις Χֵן וְדִיָּה. Ἡ Χֵן σημαίνει χάρις ἢ χάριν, καὶ ἡ דִיָּה σημαίνει Θεός ἢ Κύριος. Ἡ Χανναδιά δηλώνει αὐτή ποὺ ἔχει τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἢ αὐτή ποὺ εἶναι εὐδοκημένη παρὰ Κυρίου. Τὸ ὄνομα αὐτὸ δὲν ἀναφέρεται ρητά στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη, ἀλλὰ ἡ σημασία του εἶναι στενά συνδεδεμένη μὲ τὴν πνευματικὴ παράδοση τῆς Ἐκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Hannadia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Hannadia derivatur ex duobus verbis hebraicis: Chen et Yah. Chen significat gratiam seu gratiam, et Yah est radix quae significat Deum seu Dominum. Itaque Hannadia potest interpretari ut illa quae gratiam Dei habet seu illa cuius manus Dei est cum ea. Nomen hoc in scripturis sacris non invenitur sub hac forma, sed tamen usus eius est in traditione christiana ad describendum nexum inter hominem et Deum.

in_english.name: Hannadia
in_english.meaning: Gift of God, God's gracious one
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hannadia originates from Hebrew roots, combining 'Chen' (חֵן), meaning grace or favor, and 'Yah' (יָהּ), a shortened form of Yahweh, meaning God. Thus, Hannadia can be interpreted as 'God's gracious gift' or 'she who has God's favor.' While the exact name does not appear in the Bible, its components are biblically rooted. In Christian tradition, Hannadia symbolizes a person who embodies God's grace and mercy. The name is associated with spiritual significance, reflecting a deep connection between the individual and the divine.

data.cultural_impact: Hannah is a name of ancient Middle Eastern origin. In the Bible, Hannah is a character from the book of Samuel. She is the mother of the prophet Samuel, who anointed the first two kings of Israel, Saul and David. Hannah's story of faith and determination to give the Lord the first fruits of her son's life has resonated through the centuries, inspiring countless women and mothers.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hannah, derived from the Hebrew words 'hannah' meaning grace and 'yad' meaning hand, symbolizes the idea of giving oneself and one's gifts to God, as Hannah did with her son Samuel. This name encourages individuals to live their lives with a servant's heart, dedicating their talents and resources to God's service, and trusting that God will use them for His purposes. Additionally, Hannah is a reminder of God's faithfulness to keep His promises, as He did in Hannah's story by giving her a son after many years of prayer.
